1.q: בֶּן־שְׁמֹנֶ֤ה שָׁנָה֙ יֹאשִׁיָּ֣הוּ בְ⁠מָלְכ֔⁠וֹ וּ⁠שְׁלֹשִׁ֤ים וְ⁠אַחַת֙ שָׁנָ֔ה מָלַ֖ךְ בִּ⁠ירוּשָׁלִָ֑ם וְ⁠שֵׁ֣ם אִמּ֔⁠וֹ יְדִידָ֥ה בַת־עֲדָ֖יָה מִ⁠בָּצְקַֽת
1.note: In this verse and the next verse, the author is introducing **Josiah** as a participant in the story as the new king of **Judah**. To translate this verse, see how you translated the similar expressions in 8:26.

2.q: וַ⁠יַּ֥עַשׂ הַ⁠יָּשָׁ֖ר בְּ⁠עֵינֵ֣י יְהוָ֑ה וַ⁠יֵּ֗לֶךְ בְּ⁠כָל־דֶּ֨רֶךְ֙ דָּוִ֣ד אָבִ֔י⁠ו וְ⁠לֹא־סָ֖ר יָמִ֥ין וּ⁠שְׂמֹֽאול
2.note: The author is continuing to introduce Josiah. See how you translated the similar expressions in 3:2 and 8:18. Alternate translation: [And he did what Yahweh considered to be right, and he lived just as David his ancestor had lived, and he did not stop living that way in any regard]

Within this image, the author is using two basic directions in which Josiah could have turned, **right** and **left**, to mean every direction. If you decide to retain the image in your translation, if it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [and he did not turn away in any direction]

3.note: The author is using this phrase to introduce a new event. See how you translated it in [2:1](ta:02).
See how you translated the similar expression in 5:18. Alternate translation: [to the temple of Yahweh]

4.note: See how you translated the similar expression in 1:3. Alternate translation: [Go]

Josiah is using **complete the silver** as a common expression of his culture to mean that Hilkiah should “prepare” the silver that has been collected to be paid out to workers. In other words, he should determine the weight of the silver and put it in bags of a given weight and value. If this phrase does not have that meaning in your language, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and he shall prepare the silver to use as payment]

The expression **having been brought** is a passive verbal form. If your language would not use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that would be natural in your language. Alternate translation: [that the priests have brought into the house of Yahweh]

5.note: To translate the term “hand” here and in verse 7, see how you translated the similar expression in 12:11. Alternate translation: [into the custody of]

In this verse, the word **hand** is singular in form, but it refers to the hands of all of the men who had been appointed to supervise the work. If you decide to keep the image of a **hand** that represents custody, if it would be helpful in your language, you could use the plural form of the word. Alternate translation: [into the hands]

The expression **appointed** is a passive verbal form. If your language would not use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that would be natural in your language. Alternate translation: [the ones responsible for the house of Yahweh]

6.note: See how you translated the similar expression in 12:12. Alternate translation: [and stones that workers had cut into shape]

7.q: לֹא־יֵחָשֵׁ֣ב אִתָּ֔⁠ם הַ⁠כֶּ֖סֶף הַ⁠נִּתָּ֣ן עַל־יָדָ֑⁠ם כִּ֥י בֶ⁠אֱמוּנָ֖ה הֵ֥ם עֹשִֽׂים
7.note: If it would be more natural in your language, you could reverse the order of these phrases, since the second phrase gives the reason for the result that the first phrase describes. Alternate translation: [since they are acting in faithfulness, the silver given to their hand shall not be reckoned with them]

The expressions **give** and **shall be not reckoned** contain passive verbal forms. If your language would not use those forms, you could express the ideas in active form or in another way that would be natural in your language. Alternate translation: [you shall not reckon with them the silver you give into their hand]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **faithfulness**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [faithfully]

9.note: See how you translated the similar expression in 1:7. Alternate translation: [a report]

Shaphan is speaking of himself and his fellow officials in the third person as **Your servants** to show humility. If it would be helpful in your language, you could translate this in a humble form in the first person. Alternate translation: [We, your servants,]
See how you translated the similar expression in 12:18. Alternate translation: [the silver that was in the house]

9.q: עַל־יַד֙ עֹשֵׂ֣י הַ⁠מְּלָאכָ֔ה הַ⁠מֻּפְקָדִ֖ים בֵּ֥ית יְהוָֽה
9.note: See how you translated these same expressions in 22:5. Alternate translation: [into the custody of the doers of the work, the ones responsible for the house of Yahweh]

10.note: See how you translated the similar expression in 3:14. Alternate translation: [in the presence of the king]

11.note: See how you indicated the significance of this action in 2:12. Alternate translation: [that he tore his clothes to show his great distress]

13.note: Josiah assumes that these officials will know that by **the people**, he means the people of the city of Jerusalem. You could indicate this explicitly in your translation if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [and for the people of Jerusalem]

The expression **having been found** is a passive verbal form. If your language would not use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that would be natural in your language. Alternate translation: [this scroll that Hilkiah found]

13.q: גְדוֹלָ֞ה חֲמַ֣ת יְהוָ֗ה אֲשֶׁר־הִיא֙ נִצְּתָ֣ה בָ֔⁠נוּ
13.note: See how you translated the similar expression “the nose of Yahweh burned against Israel” in 13:3. Alternate translation: [great is the anger of Yahweh, that which is has been provoked against us]

13.q: גְדוֹלָ֞ה חֲמַ֣ת יְהוָ֗ה אֲשֶׁר־הִיא֙ נִצְּתָ֣ה בָ֔⁠נוּ
13.note: The expression **is kindled** is a passive verbal form. If your language would not use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that would be natural in your language. Alternate translation: [great {is} the heat of Yahweh, that which is burning against us] or [great is the anger of Yahweh that we have provoked]

By **did not listen to the words of this scroll**, King Josiah means that the ancestors of the Judeans did not obey what was written in the scroll. You could indicate this explicitly in your translation if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [did not do what this scroll said to do]

The expression **written** is a passive verbal form. If your language would not use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that would be natural in your language. Alternate translation: [everything that it records]

14.note: This could mean: (1) that Shallum was responsible to care for the vestments of the priests, like the official described in 10:22. Alternate translation: [the official who cared for the priests’ vestments] or (2) that Shallum was responsible to care for the king’s royal robes. Alternate translation: [the official who cared for the king’s royal robes]

The word that the ULT translates as **the Second Quarter** means “second” or “second part.” Many scholars believe that it described a newer, expanded district of Jerusalem that was built to the north of the original city as the city grew, possibly during the reign of King Hezekiah or his successors. Some translations call this the “New Quarter” or the “Second District.” If a translation of the Bible exists in your region, you may wish to use the name that it uses. If a translation of the Bible does not exist in your region, you may wish to use the name that the ULT uses.

15.q: וַ⁠תֹּ֣אמֶר אֲלֵי⁠הֶ֔ם כֹּֽה־אָמַ֥ר יְהוָ֖ה אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל אִמְר֣וּ לָ⁠אִ֔ישׁ אֲשֶׁר־שָׁלַ֥ח אֶתְ⁠כֶ֖ם אֵלָֽ⁠י
15.note: See the discussion in the introduction to this chapter of the long quotation in verses 15–20, in which there are multiple levels of quotation. If it would be clearer in your language, you could translate this verse so that there is not a quotation within a quotation. If it would be clearer in your language, you could translate this so that there is not a quotation within a quotation. Alternate translation: [And she told them, “Yahweh, the God of Israel, wants you to tell the man who sent you to me]

16.q: כֹּ֚ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה הִנְ⁠נִ֨י מֵבִ֥יא רָעָ֛ה אֶל־הַ⁠מָּק֥וֹם הַ⁠זֶּ֖ה וְ⁠עַל־יֹֽשְׁבָ֑י⁠ו אֵ֚ת כָּל־דִּבְרֵ֣י הַ⁠סֵּ֔פֶר אֲשֶׁ֥ר קָרָ֖א מֶ֥לֶךְ יְהוּדָֽה
16.note: There are four levels of quotation here. The author is quoting what Huldah said, continuing from the previous verse (level 1). This includes instructions from Yahweh, also continuing from the previous verse (level 2). These instructions include something that Yahweh wants the officials to say (level 3). And that includes a further quotation from Yahweh (level 4). Use the appropriate punctuation in your language to mark these levels of quotation. Alternatively, you could translate this so that there are not second-level or third-level quotations.

16.q: כֹּ֚ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה הִנְ⁠נִ֨י מֵבִ֥יא רָעָ֛ה אֶל־הַ⁠מָּק֥וֹם הַ⁠זֶּ֖ה וְ⁠עַל־יֹֽשְׁבָ֑י⁠ו אֵ֚ת כָּל־דִּבְרֵ֣י הַ⁠סֵּ֔פֶר אֲשֶׁ֥ר קָרָ֖א מֶ֥לֶךְ יְהוּדָֽה
16.note: If you have decided to translate all of this long quotation in such a way that there will not be quotations within quotations, you can continue doing that in this verse. Alternate translation: [that he says that he is about to bring disaster to this place and upon its inhabitants, all of the words of the scroll that the king of Judah has read]

Yahweh is speaking of himself in the third person because he is making a solemn declaration. If it would be helpful in your language, you could translate this in the first person. Alternate translation: [This is what I have to say to you]
See how you translated the similar expression in 21:12. Alternate translation: [I am about to bring disaster]

16.q: אֵ֚ת כָּל־דִּבְרֵ֣י הַ⁠סֵּ֔פֶר אֲשֶׁ֥ר קָרָ֖א מֶ֥לֶךְ יְהוּדָֽה
16.note: See how you translated the similar expression in 1:7. Alternate translation: [all of the punishments described in the scroll that the king of Judah has read]

17.q: תַּ֣חַת ׀ אֲשֶׁ֣ר עֲזָב֗וּ⁠נִי וַֽ⁠יְקַטְּרוּ֙ לֵ⁠אלֹהִ֣ים אֲחֵרִ֔ים לְמַ֨עַן֙ הַכְעִיסֵ֔⁠נִי בְּ⁠כֹ֖ל מַעֲשֵׂ֣ה יְדֵי⁠הֶ֑ם וְ⁠נִצְּתָ֧ה חֲמָתִ֛⁠י בַּ⁠מָּק֥וֹם הַ⁠זֶּ֖ה וְ⁠לֹ֥א תִכְבֶּֽה
17.note: If you have decided to translate all of this long quotation in such a way that there will not be quotations within quotations, you can continue doing that in this verse. Alternate translation: [because they abandoned him and burned incense to other gods, so that they have made him angry by all of the works of their hands. So his heat is kindled against this place, and it will not extinguish]

Yahweh is using one act of worship, burning **incense**, to mean worship in general. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and worshiped other gods]

Yahweh is using the phrase **the works of their hands** to mean the idols that the Judeans made with their **hands**. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [by all the idols that they made] or [by making all those idols]

17.q: וְ⁠נִצְּתָ֧ה חֲמָתִ֛⁠י בַּ⁠מָּק֥וֹם הַ⁠זֶּ֖ה וְ⁠לֹ֥א תִכְבֶּֽה
17.note: Here, **this place** represents the people who live in that place. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [So my heat is kindled against the people who live in this place, and it will not extinguish]

17.q: וְ⁠נִצְּתָ֧ה חֲמָתִ֛⁠י בַּ⁠מָּק֥וֹם הַ⁠זֶּ֖ה וְ⁠לֹ֥א תִכְבֶּֽה
17.note: See how you translated the similar expression in 22:13. Alternate translation: [So I have become very angry with the people who live in this place, and I will not stop being angry]

This verse is the conclusion of the second-level, third-level, and fourth-level quotations that began in the previous two verses. If you have decided to use punctuation to mark levels of quotation, end this verse with the appropriate punctuation for closing those levels of quotation.

18.q: וְ⁠אֶל־מֶ֣לֶךְ יְהוּדָ֗ה הַ⁠שֹּׁלֵ֤חַ אֶתְ⁠כֶם֙ לִ⁠דְרֹ֣שׁ אֶת־יְהוָ֔ה כֹּ֥ה תֹאמְר֖וּ אֵלָ֑י⁠ו כֹּֽה־אָמַ֤ר יְהוָה֙ אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל הַ⁠דְּבָרִ֖ים אֲשֶׁ֥ר שָׁמָֽעְתָּ
18.note: If you have decided to translate all of this long quotation in such a way that there will not be quotations within quotations, you can continue doing that in this verse. Alternate translation: [But tell the king of Judah, the one having sent you to seek Yahweh, that Yahweh, the God of Israel, says to him regarding the words that he heard]

Huldah is referring to the **words** that Josiah **heard** when Shaphan read to him from the scroll. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [regarding what the scroll said would happen if the Israelites forsook him]

19.q: יַ֠עַן רַךְ־לְבָ֨בְ⁠ךָ֜ וַ⁠תִּכָּנַ֣ע ׀ מִ⁠פְּנֵ֣י יְהוָ֗ה בְּֽ⁠שָׁמְעֲ⁠ךָ֡ אֲשֶׁ֣ר דִּבַּרְתִּי֩ עַל־הַ⁠מָּק֨וֹם הַ⁠זֶּ֜ה וְ⁠עַל־יֹשְׁבָ֗י⁠ו לִ⁠הְי֤וֹת לְ⁠שַׁמָּה֙ וְ⁠לִ⁠קְלָלָ֔ה וַ⁠תִּקְרַע֙ אֶת־בְּגָדֶ֔י⁠ךָ וַ⁠תִּבְכֶּ֖ה לְ⁠פָנָ֑⁠י וְ⁠גַ֧ם אָנֹכִ֛י שָׁמַ֖עְתִּי נְאֻם־יְהוָֽה
19.note: There are three levels of quotation here. The author is quoting what Huldah said to the officials (level 1), continuing from verse 15. This includes what the officials are supposed to say to King Josiah, continuing from the previous verse (level 2). This includes a quotation from Yahweh, which begins in this verse (level 3). Use the appropriate punctuation in your language to mark these levels of quotation. Alternatively, you could translate this so that there are not second-level or third-level quotations.

19.q: יַ֠עַן רַךְ־לְבָ֨בְ⁠ךָ֜ וַ⁠תִּכָּנַ֣ע ׀ מִ⁠פְּנֵ֣י יְהוָ֗ה בְּֽ⁠שָׁמְעֲ⁠ךָ֡ אֲשֶׁ֣ר דִּבַּרְתִּי֩ עַל־הַ⁠מָּק֨וֹם הַ⁠זֶּ֜ה וְ⁠עַל־יֹשְׁבָ֗י⁠ו לִ⁠הְי֤וֹת לְ⁠שַׁמָּה֙ וְ⁠לִ⁠קְלָלָ֔ה וַ⁠תִּקְרַע֙ אֶת־בְּגָדֶ֔י⁠ךָ וַ⁠תִּבְכֶּ֖ה לְ⁠פָנָ֑⁠י וְ⁠גַ֧ם אָנֹכִ֛י שָׁמַ֖עְתִּי נְאֻם־יְהוָֽה
19.note: If you have decided to translate all of this long quotation in such a way that there will not be quotations within quotations, you can continue doing that in this verse. Alternate translation: [that because his heart is tender and he humbled himself in his presence when he heard what he spoke against this place and against its dwellers, that they would become a horror and a curse, and he tore his clothes and wept to his face, he declares that now he, he has also heard]

Here the **heart** represents a person’s feelings and disposition. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation. You could also use plain language. Alternate translation: [your conscience is sensitive] or [you grieved for the sins of the Judeans]
See how you translated the similar expression in 3:14. Alternate translation: [in the presence of Yahweh … in my presence]

Yahweh is speaking of himself in the third person because he is making a solemn declaration. If it would be helpful in your language, you could translate this in the first person. Alternate translation: [from my face] or [in my presence]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **word**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [something that would horrify people]

Yahweh means that people would **curse** others by saying that they wanted the same thing to happen to them that had happened to the Judeans. Alternate translation: [and an example that people will use to curse others]

Yahweh is stating the pronoun **I** separately, even though the verb translated as **I have … heard** already includes this meaning. He is doing that to emphasize his personal awareness of what Josiah has done and said. If a speaker of your language would use an explicit pronoun for the same purpose, you may want to use that construction in your translation. If not, your language may have other ways of showing the meaning here. See how you translated the similar expression “I, I also know” in 2:3. Alternate translation: [for my part, I have heard]

Yahweh means implicitly that he has **heard** the humble, repentant things that Josiah has said (and also seen his acts of humility and repentance). You could indicate this explicitly in your translation if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [I have heard the humble, repentant things you have said and seen your humble, repentant actions]

Yahweh is speaking of himself in the third person because he is making an authoritative proclamation. If it would be helpful in your language, you could translate this in the first person. See how you translated the same expression in 9:26. Alternate translation: [This is what I, Yahweh, declare]

20.q: לָ⁠כֵן֩ הִנְ⁠נִ֨י אֹֽסִפְ⁠ךָ֜ עַל־אֲבֹתֶ֗י⁠ךָ וְ⁠נֶאֱסַפְתָּ֣ אֶל־קִבְרֹתֶי⁠ךָ֮ בְּ⁠שָׁלוֹם֒ וְ⁠לֹא־תִרְאֶ֣ינָה עֵינֶ֔י⁠ךָ בְּ⁠כֹל֙ הָֽ⁠רָעָ֔ה אֲשֶׁר־אֲנִ֥י מֵבִ֖יא עַל־הַ⁠מָּק֣וֹם הַ⁠זֶּ֑ה
20.note: If you have decided to translate all of this long quotation in such a way that there will not be quotations within quotations, you can continue doing that in this verse. Alternate translation: [Tell him that Yahweh says that he is going to gather him to his fathers, and he will be gathered to his graves in peace, and his eyes will not see all of the disaster that he will bring upon this place]
See how you translated the similar expression in 20:5. Alternate translation: [I am going to gather you to your fathers]
See how you translated the similar expression in 8:24. Alternate translation: [I am going to allow you to die]

Yahweh is likely using the plural form **graves** because he means that Josiah will be buried in the royal family plot, where there are many graves of earlier kings. It may be more natural in your language to use a singular form. Alternate translation: [and you will be buried in your grave] or [and you will be buried in the royal family plot]

The expression **will be gathered** is a passive verbal form. If your language would not use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that would be natural in your language. Alternate translation: [and the Judeans will bury you in your grave]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **peace**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [peacefully]

Yahweh using one part of Josiah, his **eyes**, to mean all of him in the act of potentially seeing the **disaster** that he will bring upon Jerusalem. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and you will not see] or [and you will not personally witness]

This is the conclusion of the second-level and third-level quotations that began in the previous two verses. It is also the end of the first-level quotation that began in verse 15. If you have decided to use punctuation to mark levels of quotation, end this verse with the appropriate punctuation for closing those levels of quotation.
